title: Pascal's Triangle II Problem

notes: The row index is 0-based, so rowIndex = 0 returns the first row [1].
The returned row contains exactly rowIndex + 1 integers and is symmetric.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: Row 3 is formed from the previous rows: 1, then 1 1, then 1 2 1, giving 1 3 3 1.
The first row of Pascal's triangle contains a single value, 1.
The second row contains two boundary values, both equal to 1.

content.problemStatement:
With an integer `rowIndex`, output the `rowIndex^th` (**0-indexed**) row of the **Pascal's triangle**.

In **Pascal's triangle**, each number is the sum of the two numbers directly above it as shown:

![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/0d/PascalTriangleAnimated2.gif)

**Example 1:**

```
Input: rowIndex = 3
Output: [1,3,3,1]
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: rowIndex = 0
Output: [1]
```

**Example 3:**

```
Input: rowIndex = 1
Output: [1,1]
```

**Constraints:**

* `0 <= rowIndex <= 33`

**Follow up:** Could you optimize your algorithm to use only `O(rowIndex)` extra space?

notes: All hidden inputs use the same JSON argument-array format as the samples.
All expected outputs are canonical JSON arrays with no extra whitespace.
The problem's maximum rowIndex is 33, so every returned coefficient fits in a signed 32-bit integer.
The in-place right-to-left update is the intended O(n) auxiliary-space optimization.
solution.approach: Build Pascal's row in place. Start with [1] and, for each row position, update entries from right to left using the recurrence row[j] = row[j] + row[j - 1]. Updating right to left preserves the previous-row value needed by the next position and uses only O(rowIndex) extra space.

better.description: Generate every row from row 0 through rowIndex, storing the complete triangle. Each new row is built from adjacent values in the previous row. This removes repeated recursive work but stores all earlier rows.

optimal.complexity: O(rowIndex^2) time and O(rowIndex) extra space, excluding the returned row itself.
optimal.description: Maintain only the requested row. For i from 0 through rowIndex, extend the row by one position and update from right to left: row[j] += row[j-1]. The reverse update order ensures row[j-1] still belongs to the previous iteration. After the final iteration, the array is exactly the requested Pascal row.

bruteForce.complexity: Exponential time in rowIndex in the worst case; O(rowIndex) recursion depth.
bruteForce.description: Treat each entry as a binomial coefficient computed recursively from C(n,k) = C(n-1,k-1) + C(n-1,k), recomputing the same subproblems many times. This directly mirrors Pascal's definition but has exponential running time.

followUps: Can you derive each value directly from the binomial-coefficient formula?
Why is right-to-left updating necessary for an in-place solution?
How would the implementation change if rowIndex were much larger than 33 and intermediate values could exceed 32-bit integers?
